vulnerabilities.description: API key hardcoded in source code: 'AKIA_EXAMPLE_HARDCODED_KEY_123456'. This allows any attacker with access to the repository to use the API key.
vulnerabilities.fix_explanation: Moved API key to environment variable. If API_KEY env var is not set, generates a secure random key using secrets module. Never hardcode secrets in source code.
vulnerabilities.impact: Unauthorized API access, potential data breach, credential compromise
remediation_steps: Set API_KEY environment variable in production
Rotate the hardcoded API key immediately
Scan repository history for any leaked keys
Use environment-specific configuration management

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command
vulnerabilities.description: SQL query constructed using string formatting with unsanitized user input. Allows attackers to inject arbitrary SQL commands.
vulnerabilities.original_code:
sql = "SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username LIKE '%{}%'".format(name)
cur.execute(sql)
vulnerabilities.fixed_code:
sql = "SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username LIKE ?"
cur.execute(sql, (f'%{name}%',))
vulnerabilities.fix_explanation: Uses parameterized queries (prepared statements) with placeholders. User input is passed as a parameter, not concatenated into the SQL string. This prevents SQL injection attacks.
vulnerabilities.impact: Database breach, unauthorized data access, data manipulation, complete database compromise
remediation_steps: Always use parameterized queries/prepared statements
Never concatenate user input into SQL strings
Use ORM frameworks like SQLAlchemy when possible
Implement input validation and whitelisting

vulnerabilities.description: Using pickle.loads() on untrusted user-supplied data allows arbitrary code execution. Pickle deserializes Python objects and can execute arbitrary code during the process.
vulnerabilities.fixed_code:
data = request.get_json()
if not data:
    return jsonify({"error": "Invalid JSON"}), 400
name = data.get('name', '')
vulnerabilities.fix_explanation: Replaced pickle with JSON parsing using get_json(). JSON is a safe, text-based format that cannot execute code. Added input validation and type checking.
vulnerabilities.impact: Complete system compromise, arbitrary code execution, data theft, malware installation
remediation_steps: Never use pickle for untrusted data
Use JSON or other safe serialization formats
If pickle is needed, use restricted pickle protocol
Validate all deserialized data before use

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command
vulnerabilities.description: User input directly concatenated into os.system() shell command. Allows arbitrary command execution through shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, etc.).
vulnerabilities.fixed_code:
import subprocess
safe_commands = ['echo', 'whoami', 'date']
if cmd_parts[0] in safe_commands:
    result = subprocess.run(cmd_parts, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
vulnerabilities.fix_explanation: Replaced os.system() with subprocess.run() and command whitelisting. Uses list of allowed commands. subprocess.run() doesn't invoke shell, preventing injection. Added timeout for safety.
vulnerabilities.impact: Complete system compromise, arbitrary command execution, data theft, lateral movement
remediation_steps: Avoid os.system() entirely
Use subprocess.run() with list arguments (avoid shell=True)
Implement strict command whitelisting
Never pass user input directly to shell

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Templating Engine
vulnerabilities.description: User input inserted into Jinja2 template without escaping, rendered with render_template_string(). Allows template injection and code execution.
vulnerabilities.fix_explanation: Removed render_template_string() and template injection point. Used escape() from markupsafe to escape HTML entities. Returns plain HTML instead of rendering as template.
vulnerabilities.impact: Code execution, XSS attacks, session hijacking, credential theft
remediation_steps: Never use render_template_string() with user input
Escape all user input before rendering
Use template auto-escaping features
Avoid dynamic template construction

vulnerabilities.description: User password 'password123' hardcoded in source code. Anyone with repository access can see all user passwords.
vulnerabilities.fix_explanation: Passwords replaced with bcrypt hashes using werkzeug.security.generate_password_hash(). Hashes are irreversible. Password can be set via environment variable for custom values.
vulnerabilities.impact: Credential compromise, unauthorized access, account takeover
remediation_steps: Never hardcode passwords
Use password hashing (bcrypt, argon2, scrypt)
Store passwords in secure vaults (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault)
Implement proper user management with secure password reset

vulnerabilities.description: Plain-text password comparison using == operator. Vulnerable to timing attacks and doesn't use proper password hashing.
vulnerabilities.fix_explanation: Replaced == comparison with check_password_hash() from werkzeug.security. This function uses constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks and properly validates bcrypt hashes.
vulnerabilities.impact: Timing attacks, brute-force vulnerability, weak authentication
remediation_steps: Always use proper password hashing libraries
Use constant-time comparison for sensitive data
Implement account lockout after failed attempts
Implement CAPTCHA for login forms

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-215: Information Exposure Through Debug Information
vulnerabilities.description: Flask debug mode enabled (debug=True). Exposes stack traces, source code, and allows arbitrary code execution through the interactive debugger.
vulnerabilities.fix_explanation: Debug mode controlled via FLASK_DEBUG environment variable, defaulting to False. Also bound to localhost (127.0.0.1) instead of listening on all interfaces.
vulnerabilities.impact: Information disclosure, stack trace leaks, source code exposure, interactive debugger access
remediation_steps: Disable debug mode in production
Use environment variables for configuration
Implement proper logging instead of debug output
Bind to localhost only, use reverse proxy for external access
